payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_scheduler.py::test_an_open_stacks_lower_layers_do_not_refuse_a_child_of_its_top stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/scheduler.py. The claim was "When an open `depends_on` ancestor's newest waiting task is a layer, `build_queue` exempts from the overlap refusal the open pull request of every task below that layer on its recorded predecessor chain. The witness records a three-layer stack batch whose layers declare no `depends_on`. A child of the top layer, and a grandchild that reaches it through a plain open parent, each overlap the layer one below the top and the layer two below it. Each is refused on each of those pull requests before the `stack_layers` rows exist. Each is admitted after, beside each one alone. The child is also admitted beside the top layer's own pull request, and beside all three. Both the plain scan and the `stack=True` scan read every case. Then the parent's spec is edited, so its layer sits at an older `spec_sha`. A `stack=True` scan lists the parent's own open pull request beside each lower layer. It refuses the parent as `open_pr_on_spec` and still admits the child. Without that pull request the edited parent would be kept and rerun from the default branch.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_scheduler.py::test_an_open_pr_from_another_task_refuses, tests/test_scheduler.py::test_an_open_pr_with_a_null_url_names_the_branch_not_none, tests/test_scheduler.py::test_a_stack_order_keeps_every_refusal_but_the_dependency_one, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
